hero.lead: A nation of 21 million where oil supplied 51.8% of government revenue in 2024 and rain-fed farming about 40% of GDP, now under a new four-year IMF programme.

capital.heading: Oil income, a new IMF programme, and a nation without power.

World Bank financing for roads that connect Chad’s farming regions and its neighbours, approved 18 February 2025

register.name: Water Security and Resilience Support Project (PASER)
register.detail: World Bank · IDA grant · Approved, release of 18 June 2026 · Provinces hosting refugees, N’Djamena and other vulnerable localities
register.note: About 1 million people, more than half from host and refugee communities
register.text: A grant from the International Development Association to build climate resilience by improving access to essential water infrastructure and services. It serves the water standard, where 6.3% of Chadians use safely managed drinking water, in the provinces that host refugees, N’Djamena and other vulnerable localities.

register.name: Chad Energy Access Enhancement Project (PAAET)
register.detail: World Bank · Mission 300 · 145,000 solar kits sold at subsidised rates in the 23 provinces · Feature story of 2 December 2025
register.note: Nearly $295 million; each kit, valued at $100, is sold for the equivalent of $20
register.text: World Bank financing of nearly $295 million to widen access to electricity, including solar kits sold at subsidised rates across the country. The project aims to raise access to electricity from 6% in 2018 to 30% in 2027 and to reach about 6 million Chadians, in the energy standard, the furthest from reach.

register.name: Development and Access to Finance for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Project
register.detail: World Bank · IDA grant · Approved, release of 31 October 2025 · Business Development Centre, guarantee fund, financial education
register.note: Nearly 8,000 small firms to gain access to credit; 200,000 people in financial education
register.text: A grant from the International Development Association to improve the business climate, through easier business creation and working commercial courts, a new Business Development Centre and a guarantee fund for loans to small firms. It serves the livelihood standard: 44.8% of Chadians live below the national poverty line.

register.name: Extended Credit Facility
register.detail: IMF · Approved 25 July 2025 · 48 months · SDR 455.65 million · SDR 28.04 million (about $38.5 million) disbursed on approval
register.note: The first and second reviews are not yet completed by the Executive Board
register.text: A four-year IMF arrangement of SDR 455.65 million (about $625 million, 325% of quota) that anchors the public finances behind the seven standards. Staff reached agreement on the first review in December 2025, and a mission in May 2026 made significant progress toward agreement on the first and second reviews; no Board completion was found by 23 November 2026.

register.name: Regional Engagement for Learning and Collaboration in Education (RELANCE)
register.detail: World Bank · Financing agreements signed 22 July 2025 · Mauritania and Chad · Germany through KfW
register.note: Total for Mauritania and Chad together; the share for Chad is not stated
register.text: Financing for a regional Open School in each country, which blends digital learning, in-person support and vocational training for young people outside school, and for a Regional Institute of Education in Nouakchott. It serves the education standard for more than 850,000 young people, half of them girls, across the two nations.

register.name: Chad Connectivity and Integration Project
register.text: Roads that link farming regions to markets and Chad to its neighbours.

register.name: Sahel Resiland Chad: Building Resilience through Sustainable Natural Resource Management
register.text: Restores land, water and pasture so farmers and herders can stay and earn through droughts.

register.name: N’Djamena Urban Resilience Project
register.text: Drainage and flood protection for the capital, where the river floods have displaced thousands.

register.name: African Development Bank support for reforms and development projects
register.detail: African Development Bank · Signed 20 August 2026 · Economic governance, domestic revenue, public administration and the business climate
register.note: About $14.3 million; reported by Financial Afrik, the Bank’s own release was not found
register.text: Financing from the African Development Bank for economic governance, the mobilisation of domestic revenue, the modernisation of public administration and the business climate. Domestic revenue is what pays, year after year, for the seven standards.

register.name: Afreximbank local-currency facility
register.detail: Afreximbank · Signed 5 August 2026, Cairo · Equivalent of EUR 110 million in local currency · Projects of the 2026 Finance Law
register.note: The largest financing the bank has extended to Chad
register.text: Financing for trade-enabling infrastructure projects approved in Chad’s 2026 Finance Law, the largest the bank has extended to Chad. The reports do not name the projects or the standards they serve.

register.name: SMARTED, schools for every province
register.detail: BADEA · Signed 16 June 2026, Baku · 2,848 classrooms in 665 primary schools and 95 lower-secondary schools
register.note: In all 23 provinces; reported by Tchadinfos, BADEA’s own release was not found
register.text: A financing agreement with the Arab Bank for Economic Development in Africa to build and equip 2,848 classrooms and to support curricula, teacher training and children who are vulnerable, girls and children with disabilities. It serves the education standard, where 5.6% of children read a simple text by the end of primary school.

register.name: Electricity Sector Support Project, phase two (PASET2), additional financing
register.detail: African Development Bank · Signed December 2025 · African Development Fund and Desert to Power, with Green Climate Fund support · 100,000 prepaid meters
register.note: A solar plant at the Moundou power station and an upgraded N’Djamena network
register.text: Additional financing to widen access to electricity, add clean energy and strengthen TchadElec, the national electricity company, through a solar plant at the Moundou power station, an upgraded distribution network in N’Djamena and 100,000 prepaid meters, mostly for households. It serves the energy standard, the furthest from reach.

register.name: PADIC-CVA, Mayo-Kebbi Est component
register.detail: African Development Fund, Climate Action Window · Grant · Signed December 2025
register.note: 9,600 smallholder farmers, 300 vulnerable women and 100 young people
register.text: A grant for climate resilience and agricultural productivity in Mayo-Kebbi Est, which strengthens producers’ capacity to adapt and their agricultural value chains. It serves the food and livelihood standards of smallholder farmers.

register.name: Gassi and Lamadji Solar PV Project
register.detail: African Development Bank · Approved December 2024 · EUR 20 million of loan and grant · EUR 8 million of guarantees from the African Development Fund and the Green Climate Fund
register.note: Two plants of 15 MWp near N’Djamena with a 6 MWh battery; total cost about EUR 41 million
register.text: Financing for two solar plants of 15 megawatts peak each near N’Djamena, with connection lines and a battery for the hours without sun, expected to generate about 61 GWh a year. It serves the energy standard, the furthest from reach, and is expected to lower fuel subsidies and energy imports.

register.name: Basic Education Transformation Project
register.detail: Islamic Development Bank · Signed 19 June 2026, Baku
register.text: Part of a multi-partner programme to give every Chadian child a basic education.

register.name: Three European Union financings for youth employment and eastern Chad
register.detail: European Union · Signed 6 May 2026 · Vocational training, income-generating activities, agriculture, water, energy and social infrastructure
register.note: For host communities, refugees and displaced people in the east
register.text: Three financings from the European Union for the employment of young people, especially women, through vocational training and income-generating activities, and for the resilience of people in eastern Chad. It serves the livelihood standard, and the food, water and energy standards in the provinces that host refugees.

register.name: AFD budget support for the airport runway and the cotton sector
register.detail: AFD · Signed 25 February 2026, N’Djamena · €11.6 million for the runway of Hassan Djamous airport · €3.4 million for the Cotton Sector Support Fund
register.note: Reported by Tchadinfos; the AFD’s own release was not found
register.text: General budget support from the Agence Française de Développement to consolidate macroeconomic stability, of which €3.4 million tops up the Fonds de Soutien au Secteur Cotonnier. The cotton share serves the livelihood standard in the cotton sector; the rest finances the runway of the N’Djamena airport.

register.name: Bank pool for two power plants east of N’Djamena
register.detail: Signed 23 February 2026 · CBI TD, the African Development Bank, Proparco and Bank of New York Mellon · Two plants of 15 MW each
register.note: About FCFA 59 billion; the plants are to be operated by TchadElec
register.text: A financing of EUR 90 million, about FCFA 59 billion, from four lenders for two power plants of 15 megawatts each on the eastern edge of N’Djamena, to electrify the suburbs of Koundoul and Linia. It serves the energy standard, the furthest from reach.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Oil
items.label: Of exports from oil, 2024
items.text: Oil already earns most of what Chad sells abroad; the task is to turn it into power and schools at home.
items.alt: Oil wellheads and a pipeline in the dry savanna of southern Chad

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2024
items.text: Rain-fed farms and herds that carry four in ten of every dollar the nation earns.
items.alt: Green sorghum and millet fields with grazing cattle in the savanna of southern Chad

items.name: The Land
items.label: Land area, 2024
items.text: Territory to farm, mine, power and protect.
items.alt: Sandstone towers and arches rising from the desert of the Ennedi Plateau, Chad

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.
items.alt: The Chari River winding through green floodplain near N’Djamena, Chad

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 46% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.
items.alt: A busy market street in N’Djamena with people in the distance, Chad

items.name: Association Al Salama
items.text: A women’s association in Abéché that dries meat for market in a solar dryer with battery storage, and whose takings, its members report, have doubled.

items.name: O’Nadif
items.text: Builds community-run filtration stations where families in underserved communities collect safe water daily at an affordable price, paid per use, with local women and youth trained to monitor quality and maintain the equipment.

items.name: Alma Ventures (ALMA)
items.text: Installed 127 solar-powered water pumps in rural Chad that give 67,000 people clean water, with local hygiene officers, a call centre and motorbike riders who keep the chlorine stocked.

items.name: Telemedan
items.text: Builds and sells solar-powered telemedicine kiosks, about $10,000 each, where a trained local operator connects rural patients to doctors by video for consultations of about $2 to $15; its 37 kiosks in 11 provinces serve an estimated 143,000 people.

items.name: Express Union Tchad
items.text: One of Chad’s leading microfinance institutions, which offers loans, savings and money transfers to small firms, women and rural households, financed in 2024 by a Proparco loan of 630 million CFA francs in a package arranged by IFC.
